**Summary (using latest available data, mainly 2022):**  
In Nigeria, around four in five people have at least basic drinking water, but only about one in three have safely managed sanitation, and less than one in three have safely managed drinking water.

---

### Data:

**Nigeria – Access to drinking water (national, % of population)**

- At least basic drinking water services (2021): <claim id="3b8a6e1f" policy="auto">78.0002</claim>%

- At least basic drinking water services (2019): <claim id="7fd5fb8e" policy="auto">74.7241</claim>%

- Safely managed drinking water services (2022): <claim id="69636604" policy="auto">28.984885</claim>%  
- Safely managed drinking water services (2021): <claim id="e6b53eed" policy="auto">28.421029</claim>%

- Safely managed drinking water services (2019): <claim id="a264094e" policy="auto">27.282338</claim>%

*(2023 entries exist but have null values, so 2022 is the latest year with actual data.)*

---

**Nigeria – Access to sanitation (national, % of population)**  
- At least basic sanitation services (2022): <claim id="4cdc76e6" policy="auto">46.5707</claim>%  
- At least basic sanitation services (2021): <claim id="bf2b6aa1" policy="auto">45.4492</claim>%  
- At least basic sanitation services (2020): <claim id="00d86af7" policy="auto">44.3511</claim>%  
- At least basic sanitation services (2019): <claim id="97479b6d" policy="auto">43.2768</claim>%

- Safely managed sanitation services (2022): <claim id="b05bca8b" policy="auto">31.971572</claim>%  
- Safely managed sanitation services (2021): <claim id="6b5fd9d9" policy="auto">31.287849</claim>%  
- Safely managed sanitation services (2020): <claim id="5f5a7ab9" policy="auto">30.618869</claim>%  
- Safely managed sanitation services (2019): <claim id="d419bd4f" policy="auto">29.964677</claim>%

*(Again, 2023 exists but with a null value.)*

---

### Analysis (for narrative use)

You could frame the situation in Nigeria roughly as follows (paraphrasing allowed for your article):

- **Water access is relatively widespread but not safely managed for many.**  
  Around 2022, close to four out of five Nigerians used at least basic drinking water services (about <claim id="8e2a15ef" policy="auto">79.6</claim>%), but only about three in ten had safely managed drinking water (around <claim id="69636604" policy="auto">29.0</claim>%). That implies roughly half the population relies on sources that are improved but not safely managed (for example, not on premises or not free from contamination).

- **Sanitation lags behind water.**  
  In 2022, fewer than half of Nigerians used at least basic sanitation facilities (about <claim id="4cdc76e6" policy="auto">46.6</claim>%), and only about one in three had safely managed sanitation (around <claim id="b05bca8b" policy="auto">32.0</claim>%). This means a large share of the population still lacks access to private, improved toilets with safe excreta disposal.

- **Slow but steady improvement.**  
  Between 2019 and 2022, both water and sanitation indicators show gradual gains of a few percentage points. For example, safely managed sanitation rose from about <claim id="d419bd4f" policy="auto">30.0</claim>% in 2019 to nearly <claim id="b05bca8b" policy="auto">32.0</claim>% in 2022, and at least basic drinking water increased from about <claim id="7fd5fb8e" policy="auto">74.7</claim>% to nearly <claim id="8e2a15ef" policy="auto">79.6</claim>% over the same period.

You can safely describe these as **SDG-aligned indicators**: “safely managed” corresponds to the higher SDG standard (on premises, available when needed, and free from contamination for water; and safe excreta management for sanitation), while “at least basic” is a lower threshold but still better than no or unimproved service.

---

### Sources:

- **World Bank — Health, Nutrition and Population Statistics (WB_HNP)**  
  - *People using safely managed drinking water services (% of population)* — Indicator ID: WB_HNP_SH_H2O_SMDW_ZS  
  - *People using at least basic drinking water services (% of population)* — Indicator ID: WB_HNP_SH_H2O_BASW_ZS  
  - *People using safely managed sanitation services (% of population)* — Indicator ID: WB_HNP_SH_STA_SMSS_ZS  
  - *People using at least basic sanitation services (% of population)* — Indicator ID: WB_HNP_SH_STA_BASS_ZS  

These are harmonized with WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) definitions for SDG 6.

---

If you tell me whether you need **urban vs. rural**, **gender/age**, or **state-level** angles, I can help you pull and phrase more targeted stats.

- Urban safely managed drinking water: <claim id="870268a9" policy="auto">36.05</claim>% of the urban population  
- Rural safely managed drinking water: <claim id="d325d5d6" policy="auto">22.39</claim>% of the rural population

---

**Analysis (chart concept):**

1. **Chart type:**  
   - A **line chart** with **Year** on the x‑axis and **% of population** on the y‑axis.

   - Both lines trend gently upward from 2019 to 2024.  
   - The urban line is consistently above the rural line, showing a persistent gap of roughly 13–15 percentage points.

3. **Suggested title and labels for your article:**
   - Title: **“Urban–rural gap in safely managed drinking water in Nigeria (2019–2024)”**  
   - Y‑axis: **“Population with safely managed drinking water (%)”**
